t: He diminished it; lessened it; made it deficient,
لَا بَخْسَ فِيهِ وَ لَا شَطَطَ
There is no deficiency in it nor excess.
] And it is said in the Kur [lxxii. 13],
of the reward of his actions,
(TA.) And in this sense, [as also in the next,] the verb is doubly trans. (Msb.) You say,
He diminished to him his right,
defrauded him, of a part of it.
(S, A.) And it is said in the Kur [vii. 83 and xi. 86 and xxvi. 183],
And ye shall not diminish unto men their things
]: (Msb:) or the verb in this instance has the signification next following. (TA.) ― -b2-
They defrauded one another in a sale.
(S.) It is said in the Kur [xii. 20],
And they sold him for a deficient,
for a price less than was incumbent:
accord. to Zj; because the sale of a man that has been found is unlawful. (TA.) -A2-
Land that produces herbage without being
land which is watered by the rain;
because it has deficient watering: (Mgh:) pl.
. (JK, TA.) ― -b2- Also, (TA, as from Ibn-Málik,) or ↓
, [which is more probably the correct form,] a rel. n. from
in the sense immediately preceding, explained in the T as signifying, (Mgh,) Seed-produce
that is not irrigated with water from a spring or well or the like, but only by the rain.
(TA.) It is said in a prov.,
; (S, A, K;) so runs the prov.; but accord. to Th, (S,) you may also say

applied to him who feigns himself to be of weak understanding when he is crafty and cunning. (K, TA.) The origin of the prov. was this: a man of the Benu-l-' Ambar, of Temeem, mixed his property with that of a woman, coveting the possession of it, and thinking that she was stupid, and that she did not take care of her property nor know it: then he made a division with her, after he had mixed; but she was not content with the division until she took her property: she complained of him to those in authority, so that he released himself from her by giving her what she desired of the property: and the man was reproved for his conduct; it being said to him, “ Thou cheatest a woman: is not this wrongful conduct (
)? ” whereupon he replied in the words above, which became a proverb. (Th, K, * TA.)

maqayis: الباء والخاء والسين أصل واحد، وهو النقص. قال الله تعالى: {وشروه بثمن بخس} [يوسف: 20] ، أي: نقص. ومن هذا الباب قولهم في المخ: بخس تبخيسا: إذا صار في السلامى والعين، وذلك حتى نقصانه وذهابه من سائر البدن. وقال شاعر: لا يشتكين عملا ما أنقين ... ما دام مخ في سلامى أو عين
mufradat: البخس: نقص الشيء على سبيل الظلم، قال تعالى: وهم فيها لا يبخسون [هود/ 15] ، وقال تعالى: ولا تبخسوا الناس أشياءهم [الأعراف/ 85] ، والبخس والباخس: الشيء الطفيف الناقص، وقوله تعالى: وشروه بثمن بخس [يوسف/ 20] قيل: معناه: باخس، أي: ناقص، وقيل: مبخوس أي: منقوص، ويقال: تباخسوا أي: تناقصوا وتغابنوا فبخس بعضهم بعضا.
